summary.text: Kim Cole is the Republican candidate for Michigan State Senate District 32, having defeated Max Riekse in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary; the Democratic nominee is Rebecca Amidon.
In a Ballotpedia survey, Cole said he is serving his fourth term as Mason County Sheriff after a 41-year career in law enforcement.

paragraphs.text: Cole graduated from Ludington High School and earned an associate degree from West Shore Community College in 1984.

He said in the survey that he is a past president of the Michigan Sheriffs' Association, was named its 2021 Michigan Sheriff of the Year, and sits on the board of directors of the National Sheriffs' Association.

Cole listed his campaign messages as affordability and local decision-making, support for crime victims and law enforcement, and safe schools, streets and communities, including opposition to cashless bail and support for school resource officers.
His listed endorsers include Right to Life Michigan, the Michigan Chamber, the NRA and more than 70 sheriffs.
